subject: Regional SKU exposure and fallback assignments for marketplace listings
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@cloudpartner.io>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regional SKU exposure and fallback assignments for marketplace listings

Team / Alice / Rajiv —

As we discussed in yesterday's sync, we need to finalize which SKUs we list in each cloud marketplace (AWS, Azure, GCP) and define an explicit fallback matrix for co-sell / routing when a SKU isn't available in a region. Attached is a first-pass workbook (sku-exposure-draft.xlsx) and a printable fallback PDF.

High-level asks:
- For each SKU (Host, Dedicated, Private) identify primary cloud + primary regions for Q3 launch.
- Define fallback behavior: model variant fallback, region fallback, or service-tier fallback (e.g., route to hosted API).
- Note any compliance/regulatory constraints that force a cloud choice (data residency).

Please reply with concrete assignments by EOD tomorrow so I can lock the marketplace publishing plan and update the partner playbook. Alice / Rajiv, we've included you because Acme's procurement schedule ties to which regions we list initially.

Attachments: sku-exposure-draft.xlsx, marketplace-fallback-matrix.pdf, legal-checklist-marketplace.pdf

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien | Head of Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@cloudpartner.io>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional SKU exposure and fallback assignments for marketplace listings

Connor —

Quick pass on the workbook with recommendations:

- Host (managed API): list globally on all three marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP) but set "GA" regions as: us-east-1 (AWS), eastus (Azure), europe-west1 (GCP). Reason: low friction for customers and we keep a single canonical SKU.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): initial listing on AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) and Azure (eastus2) only. GCP has limited prem availability for our preferred instance families; recommend a later staggered launch once quantized q4 kernels land.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): marketplace listing as "private offer" per cloud; region exposure should be conservative — begin with US and EU (us-east-1, europe-west1) and delay APAC until we validate KMS/HSM integrations.

Fallback matrix (short):
- If primary SKU unavailable in region, try identical SKU in partner-region on same cloud (e.g., us-east-1 -> us-west-2) with cost-aware routing.
- If same-cloud fallback fails, route to Hosted API SKU (rate-limited) as last resort with explicit SLA note.
- For Dedicated-heavy customers, offer white-glove provisioning (manual) when marketplace routing can't meet latency SLOs.

Notes / risks:
- Azure marketplace pricing parity is tricky (listing + metered plans). Need pricing ops support to ensure consistent billing.
- Legal flagged data residency controls for Acme in Germany — see legal-checklist-marketplace.pdf — might force EU-only for certain SKUs.

I'll update the spreadsheet with region tags and a confidence column.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Director, GTM Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@cloudpartner.io>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional SKU exposure and fallback assignments for marketplace listings

Thanks Karthik — adding the sales lens.

From a co-sell and procurement perspective:
- Customers like clear minimal friction: full Host SKU in the most common marketplaces drives conversion. Prioritize AWS listing first (highest signal), then Azure. GCP should be second wave but marketed as "coming soon" in co-sell decks.
- For Dedicated, we need a separate co-sell play: partner-led intro + Redwood SE kickoff. Marketplace listing alone won't close deals. We should surface a checkbox in the marketplace listing that triggers an SE task.
- Pricing: keep list price consistent across clouds where possible. If Azure forces a higher fee due to marketplace margins, flag it and we'll evaluate a reseller credit for parity.

Action items for me: update one-pager for partner teams and create a co-sell checklist tied to HS-83472.

Laura
Laura Bennett | Senior Sales Manager, Cloud GTM | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-30T17:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional SKU exposure and fallback assignments for marketplace listings

Connor / team —

Thanks for the draft. A couple of clarifying questions from Acme procurement: 
- For Germany-specific workloads we do require EU-only hosting for the Private SKU; can you confirm "private offer" will be EU-resident and not routed to US keys?
- For the Dedicated SKU, what's the expected lead time for provisioning if we fall back to manual provisioning? We need an SLA estimate for procurement approvals.

Also, can you add "eu-central-1" explicitly for Private in the spreadsheet? That's the region our compliance team will accept.

Regards,
Alice
Alice Chen | Head of Cloud Procurement | Acme Analytics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@acme-analytics.com>

Date: 2027-05-31T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional SKU exposure and fallback assignments for marketplace listings

Thanks everyone — finalizing decisions below (locking into the Drive doc). See linked HS ticket and checklist.

Decisions (Q3 marketplace launch):
- Host (Managed API): list on AWS, Azure, GCP globally. GA regions: aws(us-east-1), azure(eastus), gcp(europe-west1).
- Dedicated: initial marketplace listing on AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) and Azure (eastus2). GCP deferred until quantization kernels validated (target Q4).
- Private (Private Offer): EU residency guaranteed for EU Private SKUs — add eu-central-1 as requested by Acme. Private offers will be posted as region-scoped marketplace items (EU/US).
- Fallback matrix: same-cloud region fallback -> same-region other-cloud only for Host SKU (with cost-note) -> final fallback to Hosted API with SLA downgrade. For Dedicated fallback, manual provisioning expected: 4-6 weeks lead time (depends on capacity); we'll surface this in the marketplace listing and in the co-sell playbook.

Action items assigned: 
- Karthik: update sku-exposure-draft.xlsx with confirmed regions and confidence tags by 2027-06-02.
- Laura: publish partner one-pager and co-sell checklist; map to HS-83472 by 2027-06-03.
- Stephanie: work with Legal to confirm private-offer EU key custody and update legal-checklist-marketplace.pdf; target 2027-06-04.
- Connor: coordinate final listing windows with partners (Rajiv) and schedule marketplace listing freeze for 2027-06-10.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3SKU-exposure-draft, HubSpot: HS-83472

If no objections by Friday, I'll brief the channel and request listing approvals.

Connor
Connor O'Brien | Head of Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference
